doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Banjo breaks on the ship
summary: The neck came off the banjo at boarding and the ship's carpenter glued it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It’s sort of a leap of faith to get on the boat and, well, let’s see what happens. I heard something about your banjo broke when you got on the ship somehow.

Yes. We played on the dock as the kids were coming onboard, and then we put our instruments away and we were supposed to play at 8 o’clock that night in the lounge. So we got up to the lounge and I opened the case and I lifted the neck of the banjo and it came right off the rest of it. And there I was with strings and the banjo in two parts. Fortunately the social chairman, the Dutch guy who was in charge of us, saw my predicament. We went downstairs immediately, down in the front, the bow of the ship, to the carpenter shop. And they jabbered in Dutch and I said yeah, okay. So I came back two days later and it had been glued together and they had it in a vise and this was one of those, I don’t know, antiques, which it’s still in one piece today. And it suffered through the whole trip to Europe and all that. But talk about here we are underway, we’ve already gone out to sea and I don’t have an instrument. So I had a couple of nights off.
